solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Take northbound course and arrest highwayman

indicators.note: in a down entry going north means reading from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

blocks.note: a rut is a well-worn course or track
to pin someone down is to arrest their movement

explanation.surface: Advice to the police: head north and catch the robber.
explanation.walkthrough: TUR + PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dick Turpin was the most famous eighteenth-century English highwayman, a mounted robber on the roads.

clue.text: Extremely hard not to get worked up, sleep having been cut short

indicators.note: worked up in a down clue means pushed upwards, so the letters read from the bottom
cut short means the word loses its final letter
the sleep word has been cut open, so the turned word is inserted into the gap

blocks.note: taken as written
a siesta is an afternoon sleep

explanation.surface: It is very hard not to get irritable when your sleep has been interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having been cut' is the insertion signal and 'short' the trimming one; 'worked up' in the surface means angry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoniest is the superlative of stony, so it means hardest, like rock, or most unfeeling.

clue.text: Each program is cipher-loaded

indicators.note: something loaded has been filled, so the program word holds the cipher inside

blocks.note: an app is a computer program
a cipher is a zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Every piece of software has encryption built in.
explanation.walkthrough: Cipher here means nought rather than code. AP(O)P.
explanation.definitionFit: A pop is an informal phrase for each, as in tickets at a fiver a pop, meaning apiece.

clue.text: Confined to bed, perhaps? You bet

blocks.note: someone ill may be confined to bed
say, as in for example, perhaps

explanation.surface: A question about whether someone is bedridden, answered emphatically yes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal exclamations of emphatic agreement, meaning certainly or absolutely.

clue.text: Introduction to Magdalen's dons one career high point

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of the college name is kept
to don is to put on clothes, so the letter is wrapped in what it puts on

blocks.note: the first letter of the Oxford college
an ace is a one in cards or dice

explanation.surface: An Oxford college's fellows reach the summit of their careers.
explanation.walkthrough: Dons looks like the plural of don, a university teacher; it is the verb to put on, and 's is short for has. ACE is worn around M.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point or peak of achievement, so a career's high point is its acme.

clue.text: Drum beat a ballroom embraces

indicators.note: embraces means holds within, so the answer sits inside the run of words before it

blocks.note: spans the end of beat, a, and the start of ballroom

explanation.surface: A drumbeat fills a ballroom.
explanation.definitionFit: An atabal is a kettledrum used by the Moors, an Arabic-derived name for a drum.

clue.text: Jumped-up PC arrests one: nothing left of blooming substance!

definitions.note: adjective, of pollen; the clue uses it as a noun

indicators.note: a police officer who arrests takes someone in, so the police word holds the next pieces
jumped up in a down clue means turned upward, so the whole assembly reads backwards

blocks.note: a PC is a police constable, a cop
the Roman numeral for one
nil means nothing
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: An upstart police officer arrests someone, leaving none of a flowering substance.
explanation.walkthrough: C(I NIL L)OP, then read upwards. Jumped-up also means self-important, the surface sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Pollinic means relating to pollen, the powdery substance produced by flowers when they bloom.

clue.text: Crack army introduced folding quality

definitions.note: the special across hint: quality gives Q, and Ctrl+Q is the keyboard shortcut to quit an application

indicators.note: something introduced is brought inside, so the army abbreviation goes into the word for a crack

blocks.note: a crack is a witty remark
the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
plication is the act of folding

explanation.surface: A crack army unit brings in a new kind of folding quality, like a uniform that packs neatly.
explanation.walkthrough: In this puzzle the across clues have no ordinary definition: one word gives a letter, and Ctrl plus that letter is the shortcut for the computer command that is the answer. QUI(TA)P then PLICATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Q for quality is the letter; pressing Ctrl+Q on most computers closes the program, the command named by the answer.

clue.text: Love games breaks at work

definitions.note: the across hint: love gives O, and Ctrl+O is the shortcut to open a file

indicators.note: the games word breaks into the phrase for at work, splitting it apart

blocks.note: PE is physical education, school games
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone's romance with sport gives them breaks while they are at work.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is the letter O, as in a tennis score of nil; O(PE)N.
explanation.definitionFit: O is the letter love stands for, and Ctrl+O is the keyboard shortcut that opens a document, the command named by the answer.

clue.text: Very old earl

definitions.note: the across hint: very gives V, and Ctrl+V is the shortcut to paste

blocks.note: something old is in the past
E is the abbreviation for earl

explanation.surface: A description of an aged aristocrat: a very old earl.
explanation.walkthrough: V is the standard abbreviation for very.
explanation.definitionFit: V stands for very, and Ctrl+V is the keyboard shortcut that pastes copied material, the command named by the answer.

clue.text: Bishop reportedly took over

definitions.note: the across hint: bishop gives B, and Ctrl+B is the shortcut for bold type

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the one for took over

blocks.note: in cricket a bowler who delivered an over has bowled it

explanation.surface: A churchman, so the story goes, seized control.
explanation.walkthrough: An over is a set of six balls in cricket, so to have taken an over is to have bowled. B is the chess notation for bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: B is the abbreviation for bishop, and Ctrl+B is the shortcut that sets text in heavy type, the formatting command named by the answer.

clue.text: After breakdown, try and replenish writer's liquid potassium

definitions.note: the across hint: potassium gives K, and Ctrl+K is the shortcut to add a hyperlink

indicators.note: a breakdown leaves things in pieces, so the two fodder words are broken and rebuilt

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a writer's pen is filled with ink

explanation.surface: After a collapse, a patient is told to try to top up their liquid potassium.
explanation.walkthrough: K is the chemical symbol for potassium.
explanation.definitionFit: K is potassium's chemical symbol, and Ctrl+K is the word-processor shortcut that adds a web link, the command named by the answer.

clue.text: Hats off to Starmer, keeping away the aristocracy

definitions.note: plural noun for upper-class people collectively

indicators.note: a hat sits on top, so taking the hats means taking the first letters of the following words
keeping means holding on to, so the two letters hold the word for away

blocks.note: the first letters of the two words
away and off both mean gone

explanation.surface: A salute to Prime Minister Starmer for keeping the upper classes at bay.
explanation.walkthrough: Hats off to is a salute; here it means take the tops of 'to Starmer'. Toff is British slang for an upper-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffs is British slang for posh, upper-class people, so collectively they are the aristocracy.

clue.text: Some time left to bottle up fragrant resin

indicators.note: some means a part of, so the answer is a stretch of letters inside the next words
bottled up in a down clue means pushed upwards, so the stretch reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters inside the two words

explanation.surface: A little time remains to store away a perfumed gum.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is an aromatic resin from tropical trees, used in varnishes and perfumes.

clue.text: Jay Gatsby's back, hardly one furlong ahead

definitions.note: the across hint: Jay gives J, and Ctrl+J is the shortcut to justify text

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, so only the end of the novel's title is kept
ahead says the run of short pieces goes in front of the single kept letter

blocks.note: just as in only just, barely
the Roman numeral for one
F is the abbreviation for furlong
the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: A racing report: Jay Gatsby is back in the field, barely a furlong in front.
explanation.walkthrough: Jay Gatsby is the hero of Fitzgerald's novel; here Jay is only the letter J. JUST + I + F go ahead of the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: J is how Jay is spelled as a letter, and Ctrl+J is the shortcut that aligns text to both margins, the command named by the answer.

clue.text: Off the point, Rex has departed far from happy

indicators.note: something that has departed is gone, so the king's letter is removed

blocks.note: a remark off the point is unrelated
R for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: The king has gone, and someone is out of sorts and very unhappy.
explanation.definitionFit: Elated means overjoyed, so unelated means not elated, a long way from happy.

clue.text: Someone selling doctor heroin

definitions.note: the across hint: heroin gives H, and Ctrl+H is the shortcut for find and replace

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
to doctor a drink is to lace it

explanation.surface: A drug dealer cuts a supply of heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: H is slang for heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: H is street slang for heroin, and Ctrl+H is the shortcut that opens find-and-replace, the command named by the answer.

clue.text: Texan county cop's sadly fracturing leg?

indicators.note: sadly means badly or wretchedly, so the letters are left in a poor order
fracturing means breaking into, so the jumbled letters split the leg word

blocks.note: a leg is a limb
the anagram fodder, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A Texas police officer may have broken someone's leg, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipscomb County is one of the 254 counties of Texas, in the far north of the Panhandle.

clue.text: King trained fighters here, boxing resort

definitions.note: the across hint: King gives R, and Ctrl+R is the shortcut to reload a web page

indicators.note: trained suggests drilled into a new formation, so the letters of the two words are rearranged
boxing means putting inside a box, so the reworked letters enclose the resort

blocks.note: the anagram fodder
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: A monarch's soldiers were drilled here, at a resort with a boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: R is Rex, Latin for king. The reworked letters split around SPA.
explanation.definitionFit: R stands for Rex, the Latin for king, and Ctrl+R is the browser shortcut that reloads the page, the command named by the answer.

clue.text: Tortoise not one to set about potato cakes

definitions.note: rösti is a single dish, the clue treats it as plural

indicators.note: not means without, so the named pair of letters is left out
set about suggests rearranged or turned around, so the remaining letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written
one of the two TO sequences in the animal's name

explanation.surface: A tortoise refuses to tuck into a plate of fried potato.
explanation.walkthrough: TORTOISE has two TO pairs; dropping the first leaves RTOISE for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Rösti is a Swiss dish of grated potato fried into a flat cake.

clue.text: Well before time, did you say, in a spin?

indicators.note: asking what you said points to the way a phrase sounds when spoken

blocks.note: well ahead of time is too early

explanation.surface: Someone flustered asks whether they have arrived far too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a twirly is a pensioner who tries to use a free bus pass too early in the morning, which may be the setter's private joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Twirly describes something twirling, turning round and round, so it is spinning.

clue.text: 9 games with second halves cancelled

indicators.note: cancelling the second half of each word means only its front portion survives

blocks.note: two games: a game and ping-pong

explanation.surface: A list of games with the latter parts called off.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 is a cross-reference: the answer to 9-across stands in as the definition. The two games are an ordinary game and ping-pong; a blog commenter preferred gaga for the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaping means wide open, like a gaping hole or a gaping mouth.

clue.text: Special cycling routes

definitions.note: the across hint: special gives S, and Ctrl+S is the shortcut to save

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the last letter rotates to the front of the word

blocks.note: Aves is an abbreviation for avenues, which are routes

explanation.surface: Dedicated bike lanes: special cycling routes.
explanation.walkthrough: AVES with its final S moved to the front. S abbreviates special, as in SAS (Special Air Service).
explanation.definitionFit: S is a standard abbreviation for special, and Ctrl+S is the keyboard shortcut that stores your work, the command named by the answer.

clue.text: Run section off page

definitions.note: the across hint: page gives P, and Ctrl+P is the shortcut to print

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the section letter is removed from the word for run

blocks.note: to sprint is to run fast
S is an abbreviation for section

explanation.surface: An instruction to a typesetter: let this part of the text overrun the page.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the abbreviation for page.
explanation.definitionFit: P abbreviates page, and Ctrl+P is the keyboard shortcut that sends a document to the printer, the command named by the answer.

clue.text: A noble look

blocks.note: first meaning: a member of the nobility, a lord
second meaning: to gaze closely or with difficulty

explanation.surface: A glance at an aristocrat.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the British House of Lords nobility, and to peer is to look closely.

clue.text: Not for eating in African land

blocks.note: first meaning: takeaway food is ordered ...
second meaning: a West African republic

explanation.surface: A takeaway order in some African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Food ordered 'to go' is taken away rather than eaten on the premises, and Togo is a country in West Africa.

clue.text: Like Mistress for Marvell to stay quiet about

definitions.note: the across hint: about gives C (circa), and Ctrl+C is the shortcut to copy

indicators.note: to stay something is to hold it in place, so the outer word holds the quiet letter

blocks.note: Andrew Marvell's poem is To His Coy Mistress
p for piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A lover, like Marvell's mistress, chooses to keep quiet about something.
explanation.walkthrough: C is circa, Latin for about, as in c. 1650. CO(P)Y.
explanation.definitionFit: C is short for circa, meaning about, and Ctrl+C is the shortcut that duplicates selected material, the command named by the answer.

clue.text: European Union monitors suspect altering name

definitions.note: the across hint: European gives E, and Ctrl+E is the shortcut to centre text

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or not to be trusted, so the word altering is not in its true order
monitors watch over all sides of something, so the bonding word surrounds what follows

blocks.note: to cement is to unite; cement makes a union
the anagram fodder
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: The European Union is watching a suspect who changed their name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European Union' reads as one body, but European is only the hint letter E and Union is the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: E abbreviates European, and Ctrl+E is the shortcut that sets text in the middle of the line, the command named by the answer.
